## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** at `31d682d`, the change fixes the case reported in #9167 when `kitty.conf` has an active `font_family` line. Explicit `bold_font`, `italic_font` and `bold_italic_font` lines follow the new family. `auto` values, commented lines and absent face lines are left alone. In isolated runs of the script, names containing sed metacharacters (`A&B/C\D Mono`), tab and indentation variants, and a symlinked `kitty.conf` were also handled correctly. The new stale-faces test fails against the base script (`not ok - font command updates stale bold face`) and passes on the PR head.

One gap remains on the other branch of the same `if`, plus a behavior change for maintainers to confirm.

### Faces stay stale when `kitty.conf` has no active `font_family`

The face loop sits inside the branch that runs only when an active `font_family` line already exists. Without one, the script appends `font_family` and never reaches the loop:

```text
kitty.conf before                 after `omarchy font set "Test Font"`
--------------------------------  ------------------------------------
# font_family JetBrainsMono ...   # font_family JetBrainsMono ...
bold_font Old Font                bold_font Old Font        <- still stale
                                  font_family Test Font     (appended)
```

**Impact:** the shipped `config/kitty/kitty.conf` template has `font_family` commented out, so a user on the current template who adds a face override by hand gets the #9167 symptom on the first font change. A second run syncs the face, because `font_family` exists by then.

**Suggested change:** compute `kitty_font_name` before the `if`, and run the face loop after the `if`/`else` so it covers both branches. On a newly created file the loop does nothing. A test case with `bold_font Old Font` and no `font_family` would cover this path.

### Deliberate per-face choices are overwritten

Every non-`auto` face line is replaced with the bare family name, not only lines that refer to the previous font. For example, `italic_font Victor Mono` alongside a different `font_family` becomes the new family. A kitty font spec such as `bold_font family="Other Family" style=Heavy`, the key/value form written by `kitten choose-fonts`, is replaced with the bare new family name, dropping the chosen family and style. The PR description lists what is deliberately left untouched but does not mention this.

**Impact:** users who picked a different face on purpose lose that choice on the next `omarchy font set`, with no backup. This is consistent with the alacritty branch of the same script, which rewrites every `family = "..."` entry, so it may well be intended.

**Suggested change:** confirm the intended scope in the PR description. One alternative is to write `auto` instead of the family name. In kitty 0.49.1 source, `auto` also inherits the regular face's font features and derives bold/italic from a variable font's axes, and an `auto` line cannot go stale on a later `font_family` edit. A narrower alternative is to rewrite only face lines that name the old family. Whether a bare family name renders differently from `auto` was assessed from source only. No rendering difference was observed or tested.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of the diff, `bin/omarchy-font-set`, the test file and kitty 0.49.1 (the version Arch ships) config and font-resolution source. The PR's `kitty-config-test.sh` and focused edge-case configs were run against both the base and head scripts in an isolated sandbox with a synthetic home directory and stubbed `fc-list`/`pkill`. kitty itself was not installed there, so its native config-parser check was skipped, and actual font rendering was not tested. `./test/cli` and the full `./test/shell` suite were not run. Faces set in `include`d files are not followed by the script, the same as the existing `font_family` handling.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, independent Opus 5.5 Xhigh and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
